records.text: This is a very niche industry that implies major government contracts, likely the CIA. There are even certain valves that are exclusively manufactured in Israel
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And by niche, I mean that you asserted that it implies major government contracts, likely the CIA. Those of you who have worked at those industries telling me that there are even certain valves that are exclusively manufactured in Israel, and that they tend to be involved in this.

verification.notes: The transcript attributes these assertions to unnamed audience emails and identifies no valve type, manufacturer, contract, or source. Current industry material confirms that Israeli firms make specialized valves and that some valve technologies have dual-use or government applications, but it does not establish that the industry generally implies CIA contracts or identify an unspecified valve exclusively manufactured in Israel. The compound claim therefore cannot be resolved.

records.text: Caldera Engineering's website says it has done engineering projects in Israel, marked by two dots on its project map
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And that even, by the way, on Caldera's website, they noted that they have worked in Israel. They have a map that they note every country that they have done engineering projects in. And one of them, or two dots, are in Israel.

verification.notes: Searches of Caldera Engineering's website (calderaengineering.com) and related pages do not reveal any map showing engineering projects by country, nor any mention of work in Israel or dots representing projects there. Multiple site pages, including About Us, History, and Engineering sections, were reviewed with no reference to Israel or such a map. Additional searches for variations like project maps or international collaborations also yielded no supporting evidence, contradicting the claim.

verification.notes: The tipster and employee are unnamed, so the claimed resume, education, acting work, and absence of engineering experience cannot be matched to a specific person. Caldera's public site does not identify enough employee history to test the anonymous allegation.

records.text: Owens said an emailed link listed an Israeli individual as Caldera Engineering's founder, but she explicitly said the team had not corroborated the listing and it could be a scraping error.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Then somebody emailed us, and this was strange. We have not been able to corroborate this. We can tell you the link was real. But we don't know if the internet was scraping and got things incorrect, but there was an Israeli individual who was listed as the founder of Caldera Engineering. We obviously know that Caldera Engineering had said that they did projects—going with their website—in Israel. I don't know what projects they worked on. We weren't able to corroborate currently that that individual is still working with the company. We don't know if this was accidental. Sometimes the internet can do some funny things and scrape and put information where it doesn't belong.

verification.notes: Owens expressly described the emailed listing as uncorroborated and possibly caused by scraping. The underlying URL or archived page is not identified in the statement or transcript, and current public company material says Caldera was founded by a group of engineers without naming the alleged Israeli individual. The cited listing cannot be authenticated.

sources.title: About Us - Caldera Engineering
sources.relevance: Current company history says Caldera was founded in 1997 by a group of engineers but does not identify the person from the uncorroborated listing.

records.text: Owens said early Caldera Engineering trademark documents showed the company used an Arizona lawyer whom Tyler Bowyer had introduced to her and whom she had hired.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Something else that was really interesting—as I was looking into Caldera Engineering—was that they opted to, in their very early years of their company, use a lawyer for trademark purposes down in Arizona, right? And I'm looking at these early documents, and I'm like, "Wait a second, I know this lawyer." This lawyer was introduced to me by Tyler Bowyer at Turning Point USA. I've worked with this lawyer. I paid this lawyer. This is crazy. So what is the pipeline between Utah and Phoenix? I don't know.

verification.notes: Trademark records confirm that Caldera Engineering filed its CALDERA application in 1998 using attorney John H. Platt. Platt's firm identifies him as a Phoenix attorney, and a separate USPTO filing shows that he represented Candace Owens LLC in 2019. These records support the documentary connection, but they do not independently establish Owens's private assertion that Tyler Bowyer introduced her to Platt.
